newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan-May overseas financing up 4.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan-May overseas financing up 4.9 pct.

text.p: South Korea said on Thursday its overseas financing in the first five months of this year rose 4.9 percent to $5.11 billion from $4.87 billion a year earlier.
The central Bank of Korea said overseas fund-raising by South Korea's financial institutions in the January-May period rose 21.6 percent to $3.71 billion from $3.05 billion.
Private-sector firms raised $1.4 billion overseas in the period, down 23.1 percent from $1.82 billion a year before.
"The collapse of Hanbo in January was believed to have affected private companies' overseas financing more seriously," said an official at the bank's international division.
Hanbo Steel Co, one of South Korea's leading steel makers, went insolvent after piling up $5.8 billion in debts, most of which were used to expand a steel mill.
The central bank said overseas fund-raising through bond issues in the January-May period totalled $4.66 billion, up slightly from $4.63 billion a year ago.
Bank and commercial loans borrowed overseas totalled $450 million in the five-month period, up from $240 million a year ago, the central bank said.
It said overseas financing in the June-July period would rise to $2.63 billion from $1.84 billion a year earlier according to plans received by the bank.
